title: Check yourself: Graph-based, model-driven and typed frameworks

questions.stem: A bank's loan flow must always check identity, then credit, then ask a person to approve, and an interrupted application must not repeat the credit check. Which style fits?

options.text: A single prompt, because the order is stated in the text of the call
options.says: Ruled out because a prompt keeps no state, and the page gives the graph, not the prompt, the job of resuming: "the run resumes from the last checkpoint".

options.text: A model-driven loop, because the model picks each next step on its own
options.says: Ruled out because the table gives the next step to "The model, at each turn", and the loan order must always be fixed.

options.text: A typed agent, because the loan is a record of fixed shape and size
options.says: Ruled out because a typed agent has "Validated output" but "Types guard the edges of the model's freedom. They do not choose the route."

options.text: A graph, because each node saves state and resumes after a stop
options.says: The page says "Checkpointers persist a thread's graph state as checkpoints", and a resumed run "repeats no earlier node", so the credit check is not paid for twice.

questions.stem: A support agent starts receiving a kind of request that its authors never listed. Which style copes without anyone adding a path for it?

options.text: A loop in which the model chooses each next step
options.says: The page says "The route is whatever the model chooses, so the same code handles a case nobody planned for."

options.text: A graph whose edges pick the next node from the state
options.says: Ruled out because "a case you did not draw has no path", and the edges are drawn in advance.

options.text: A typed agent whose replies must fit an output schema
options.says: Ruled out because "Types guard the edges of the model's freedom. They do not choose the route."

options.text: A checkpointer that restores the run to its last state
options.says: Ruled out because "A checkpoint is a copy of the state at a point in the graph.", which helps a run resume and adds no path.

origin.section: Model-driven: the model draws the route

questions.stem: A model-driven loop keeps calling the same tool and never produces a final reply. Which control does the engineering post name for this?

options.text: A checkpoint saved after each tool call
options.says: Ruled out because "A checkpoint is a copy of the state at a point in the graph.", which saves the state and does not end a loop.

options.text: A longer context window for the whole conversation
options.says: Ruled out because "a loop that never ends must be cut off", and a larger window does not give the loop an end.

options.text: A ceiling on the number of rounds that it is allowed
options.says: The post lists "stopping conditions (such as a maximum number of iterations) to maintain control."

options.text: A second model that repeats each call to confirm it
options.says: Ruled out because a repeated call adds cost without a stop, and "Agentic systems often trade latency and cost for better task performance".

origin.section: Model-driven: the model draws the route
